inputs.proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.
inputs.original_proposal: Core needs no global setup: ecuio_init and ecuio_shutdown become optional no-ops, init always returns ECUIO_OK, and the bridge and QML drop the coreInitialized gate.

questions: Has the author verified that the library truly has no global state requiring thread-safe initialization? The removal of g_initialized needs careful analysis.
What is the full concurrency model of the library? Are there other global resources that might need initialization?
The comment says 'A caller may pair them, call either any number of times, or never call them' - does this mean the old code's compare_exchange_strong was unnecessary if it always returned ECUIO_OK?
Is there any code in the library that checks g_initialized before proceeding? If not, why was it there?
The bridge code (qttunebridge.cpp) now ignores the return value of ecuio_init() - is this safe given the library's new contract?

claim: C ABI integrity concern: The header comment states 'Both calls are optional and do nothing; init always returns ECUIO_OK' but this changes the library's contract. Callers may have code that checks the return value or relies on the initialization/shutdown semantics. Making these no-ops could break existing code that was written for the original semantics.; file: core/include/ecuio/core.h; quote: ecuio_status_t ecuio_init(void);
void ecuio_shutdown(void);
nits: The header comment in core.h could be more precise about what 'optional' means - does it mean the calls are truly no-ops or just that they don't affect functionality?
The profile.h comment change removes the phrase 'independent of ecuio_init' which might be important documentation about the library's behavior without init.
Consider adding a static_assert or compile-time check to verify the library truly has no global state requiring initialization.
